Korea Travel Tips 2026: Everything You Need to Know Before You Go

Essential Korea travel tips for first-time visitors: money, SIM cards, etiquette, safety, apps, and everything in between.

⏱ 10 min read · 🇰🇷 Seoul, Korea · Updated 2026

Korea Travel Tips — The Real Stuff Nobody Tells You

Korea is one of the easiest countries to travel in Asia — efficient public transport, safe streets, incredible food, and friendly locals. But like any destination, there are things that will make your trip dramatically smoother if you know them in advance. Here's everything you actually need.

💳 Money & Payments

Korea is rapidly going cashless, but cash still matters in some places. Here's what you need to know:

  • Currency: Korean Won (KRW / ₩). ₩1,000 ≈ $0.75 USD
  • ATMs: 7-Eleven and GS25 convenience store ATMs accept foreign cards reliably. Airport ATMs work 24/7.
  • Credit cards: Accepted almost everywhere in Seoul. Visa and Mastercard widely accepted.
  • Cash needed for: Traditional markets (Gwangjang, Namdaemun), small restaurants, pojangmacha tents, and some taxis
  • Tipping: Not customary in Korea. Don't tip — it can cause confusion.
💡 Currency exchange tip: The best rates are at Myeongdong street money changers or banks. Avoid hotel and airport exchange booths — the rates are terrible. Withdraw won from ATMs if you need cash quickly.

📱 SIM Cards & Internet

Korea has some of the world's fastest and most reliable mobile internet. You have three options:

  • Tourist SIM: Available at Incheon Airport arrivals hall. KT, SK Telecom, LG U+ all offer tourist SIMs. 5–10 days of unlimited data for ₩25,000–₩55,000.
  • eSIM: The easiest option if your phone supports it. Buy before you leave home from Airalo or Klook. No queuing at the airport.
  • Pocket WiFi: Good for groups. Rent at the airport or pre-order for delivery to your hotel.
💡 Pro tip: Get an eSIM before you leave home. You'll have data the second you land — helpful for navigation from the airport. Airalo Korea plans start around $8 for 1GB.

🚇 Getting Around

Seoul's public transport is world-class and extremely affordable.

  • T-money card: Rechargeable transit card for subway and buses. Buy at any convenience store for ₩3,000, then top up. Saves ₩100 per ride vs cash fare.
  • Subway: 9 lines covering almost everywhere you want to go. Signs in English. Apps: Naver Maps, Kakao Maps, or Seoul Metro.
  • Bus: Color-coded system. Blue = long distance, Green = neighborhood, Yellow = city center circular, Red = express to suburbs.
  • Taxi: Affordable and plentiful. Use Kakao T app to hail — you can type your destination in English. Base fare ₩4,800.
  • KTX (high-speed rail): Seoul to Busan in 2.5 hours for about ₩59,000.

🏨 Where to Stay

Seoul's neighborhoods each have a very different vibe. Choose based on what you want:

  • Myeongdong: Best for first-timers. Central, tons of shopping, good transport links.
  • Hongdae: Young, creative, nightlife. Great for solo travelers and couples.
  • Insadong/Bukchon: Traditional culture, quieter, beautiful.
  • Gangnam: Upscale, modern, great restaurants. More expensive.
  • Itaewon: International, diverse food, expat community.

🙏 Korean Etiquette

Koreans are polite and forgiving of tourist mistakes, but knowing the basics earns genuine respect:

  • Shoes off: Always remove shoes when entering a home and many traditional restaurants.
  • Two hands: Give and receive objects (especially business cards, money, drinks) with two hands or with your right hand supported by your left.
  • Elders first: Let older people sit first, exit the elevator first, be served first.
  • Quiet on the subway: Koreans are remarkably quiet on public transport. Keep phone calls brief and voices low.
  • Don't tip: Seriously — it's not done here.
  • Pouring drinks: Don't pour your own drink. Pour for others and wait for them to pour for you.
💡 Language tip: Learn 5 Korean phrases and locals will love you: 감사합니다 (gamsahamnida — thank you), 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo — hello), 주세요 (juseyo — please give me), 얼마예요? (eolmayeyo — how much?), 화장실 (hwajangsil — bathroom).

📲 Essential Apps for Korea

  • Naver Maps: Better than Google Maps for Korea. Real-time transit, walking routes, English available.
  • Kakao T: Taxi app. Works in English. Essential.
  • Papago: Best translation app for Korean (by Naver). Better than Google Translate for Korean.
  • Baemin / Coupang Eats: Food delivery apps. Order to your hotel.
  • KakaoTalk: Everyone in Korea uses this. Download it — some restaurants and services communicate via KakaoTalk.

🌡️ Best Time to Visit

  • Spring (March–May): Cherry blossoms, mild weather. Most popular season. Book accommodation early.
  • Summer (June–August): Hot and humid. Monsoon rains in July. Great for summer festivals.
  • Autumn (September–November): Stunning fall foliage. Perfect weather. Second most popular.
  • Winter (December–February): Cold but dry. Christmas lights, skiing, and fewer tourists.

🛂 Visa & Entry

Citizens of 112 countries can enter Korea visa-free for stays up to 90 days (including USA, UK, EU, Australia, Canada). K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization) was required but has been suspended for most countries through 2025 — check the latest requirements before you travel. Passport must be valid for the duration of your stay.

🏥 Health & Safety

Korea is extremely safe. Violent crime against tourists is virtually unheard of. The biggest risks are:

  • Getting lost (use Naver Maps)
  • Overheating in summer (stay hydrated)
  • Drinking too much soju (it sneaks up on you)

Medical care is excellent and relatively cheap. Most major hospitals have international clinics with English-speaking staff. Travel insurance is recommended but not legally required.
